CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

These agents are indicated for **cardiorenal protection even when A1c is already at goal**:
- Type 2 diabetes **plus atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)**: add a GLP-1 RA or an SGLT2
  inhibitor to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus heart failure**: add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** to reduce heart-failure hospitalization.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus chronic kidney disease** (eGFR ≥ 20): add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** for renal protection.
The decision is **outcome-driven, not glucose-driven**: a patient at an A1c goal on metformin alone who has
CKD with albuminuria should still have an SGLT2 inhibitor added for renal protection — a recommendation no
HEDIS quality measure captures.

Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 ≥1 HbA1c test in the measurement year Good control < 8.0%; poor control > 9.0%; general target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

This protocol governs quality measurement and care escalation for adults with diabetes mellitus , identified by an ICD-10-CM diagnosis in the E10 (type 1), E11 (type 2), or E13 (other specified) families, including all descendant codes (e.g. E11.21 Type 2 diabetes with diabetic nephropathy , E11.319 … with unspecified diabetic retinopathy ). Effective **measurement year 2026**, the Glycemic Status Assessment (GSD) numerator accepts a **Glucose
Management Indicator (GMI)** derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) as an equivalent glycemic-status
result, alongside a laboratory **HbA1c**. The GMI result is identified by **LOINC 97506-0**; HbA1c remains
**LOINC 4548-4** (and method variants). A patient with a qualifying GMI but no lab HbA1c is now **compliant**.
Operational impact: the GSD value set gains a code for MY2026. A patient who looked like a care gap under the
MY2025 value set (CGM data only, no lab draw) flips to compliant under MY2026 — a pure **measure-drift** event
driven by a value-set version change, not by any change in the patient's data.

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

Start an **ACE inhibitor or ARB** when a patient has hypertension with albuminuria, or chronic kidney disease.
The albuminuria gate is a **urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR) ≥ 30 mg/g**. Monitor uACR **at least
annually**. The KED measure checks that an eGFR test *and* a uACR test were done; it does not encode the
ACE/ARB decision that an abnormal uACR should trigger.

Patients with **pre-existing diabetes** (already under diabetes management), hospice, or death during the
measurement year are excluded; a patient with no antipsychotic dispensing is not eligible.

## Definition
**Subsumption** is the "is-a" relationship between a broader concept and its narrower descendants. For example, `E11.21` *Type 2 diabetes with diabetic nephropathy* **is a** `E11` *Type 2 diabetes mellitus*. Querying by a parent concept should include all of its descendants.

## Structures
* **Adjacency** (`icd10_hier`): each code with its immediate parent. Rolling up requires a recursive query.
* **Transitive closure** (`icd10_closure`, `rxnorm_closure`): every `(ancestor_code, descendant_code)` pair at all depths (depth 0 = self). Membership becomes a **single equality join** with no recursive CTE, which is fast, portable, and easy for Genie to generate.

## Examples
* **Diagnoses:** E10/E11/E13 → every specific diabetes code (**Diabetes Cohort**).
* **Medications:** statin ingredients → their clinical-drug codes (**SPD**).

## Business use
This is meaning via hierarchy, not flat code lists: specific codes are included automatically, without anyone maintaining them.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months.
